compliance.why_it_matters: A claim can be denied without written evidence.

compliance.check: Work equipment over the immediate-deduction limit
compliance.why_it_matters: Items over the limit are depreciated over their effective life, and only the work-use share counts.
Renovating or replacing a whole asset is usually a capital improvement, not a deductible repair.
Only gifts to registered charities, with a receipt, are deductible. Crowdfunding for a person usually is not.

compliance.check: Rental property ran at a loss (prior year)
compliance.why_it_matters: A rental loss is allowed, but keep every record that supports it.
A gap means a missing pay or a deposit in the wrong category.
They are left out of budgets and tax totals until categorised.
A typo in a category ID drops the row from every view.
Same merchant, amount, account and day. Usually a double charge worth disputing.

compliance.check: Transfers that do not net to zero
compliance.why_it_matters: A one-sided transfer means an account feed is missing.
Interest means the card was not paid in full that month.
Rows dated after the as-of date are left out of every view.

compliance.check: Valuations missing for the as-of date
compliance.why_it_matters: Property, super, shares, the car and both loans read as zero until their month-end values are entered, so net worth and the mortgage are wrong.
compliance.where_to_look: Valuations, one row per item in Assets

compliance.check: Salary deposits without a payslip (current year)
compliance.why_it_matters: Gross pay and tax withheld come from payslips, so the tax forecast is wrong until every pay has one.

compliance.check: Bank import missing for the latest month
compliance.why_it_matters: An everyday account or card with no rows this month usually means its statement was not imported.

compliance.check: Subscriptions charged but not on the list
compliance.why_it_matters: A new subscription, often a free trial that rolled into a paid plan, is invisible to the usage and price checks until it is on the list.
Usually the same statement imported twice. Views look rows up by ID, so every ID must be used once.

A transfer needs a mate of the opposite amount on another account within four days; one without means a feed is missing or a payment was categorised as a transfer. Paired transfers never count as spending.
The month's change across every balance must equal income less spending plus valuation changes. Anything left over is a transfer with no mate, a row on the wrong account or a missing statement.
